clue.text: Shape spin-doctor gives feel-good factor

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political spin-doctor shapes the message so that voters feel good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin-doctor' reads as one job, but the hyphen splits it: 'doctor' rearranges SHAPE SPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Contentment is the overall feel-good state a person enjoys.

clue.text: If Buddhist leader went back to Italian resort…

indicators.note: going back means the run of if followed by the lama is read from end to start

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or leader

explanation.surface: A holiday conditional: if the Dalai Lama travelled back to the Italian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went back' turns IF + LAMA as one run, giving AMAL then FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Campanian coast south of Naples, famous as a holiday destination.

clue.text: …he could take this boat on the po — deal is arranged

indicators.note: arranging the letters means the words po and deal are reordered

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, the lama could hire a little boat on the River Po once a deal is struck.
explanation.walkthrough: The Po is Italy's longest river, and the ellipsis joins this clue to the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pleasure craft propelled by pedals, hired at resorts.

clue.text: The hard bit for teachers? Eating scrambled egg!

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are mixed up, so the letters of egg are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher's tricky breakfast question about the tough part of a scrambled egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hard bit' sounds like a schoolroom difficulty, but it is a lump of gold; the teachers are a British union, the National Union of Teachers, and 'scrambled' makes GGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump of gold or other solid matter is a small hard piece.

clue.text: Laurel adopts church's attitudes

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy
CE is the Church of England, so the possessive gives CE plus S

explanation.surface: A man called Laurel takes on the views of his church.
explanation.definitionFit: Positions or standpoints taken on an issue.

clue.text: You can squeeze a tune out of it

definitions.text: You can squeeze a tune out of it

parts.words: You can squeeze a tune out of it
parts.note: read literally: an instrument with bellows that are pressed in and out to make music

explanation.definitionFit: A box-shaped wind instrument played by pressing bellows together, with keys or buttons.

clue.text: Alan, being male, gets a maid in Bahrain

indicators.note: Alan being round male is read as the name holding the letter for male within it

parts.note: taken as written
an amah is a maid or nursemaid in East and South Asia

explanation.surface: A man named Alan acquires a housemaid while living in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: AMAH, an Asian word for a nursemaid, may be unfamiliar.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the Gulf island state, also known simply as Manama.

clue.text: Is nothing there? Surely the start of contour lines?

parts.note: taken as written
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of Surely

explanation.surface: A doubtful map-reader wonders whether those faint marks really are contour lines.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map these join places sharing the same average summer temperature.

clue.text: Fish on little plates? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: Fish on little plates? Quite the opposite

parts.words: Fish on little plates? Quite the opposite
parts.note: rather than fish served on small plates, think of the small plates covering a fish's body

explanation.definitionFit: The thin overlapping plates protecting the skin of a fish.

clue.text: A graduate on the way to Riga's new carnival

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
RD is short for road, a way

indicators.note: new shows the letters of Riga's are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A graduate travelling to Latvia's capital for its new festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way to' suggests travel, but 'on' simply places one piece before the next and 'to' is a link; 'new' gives IGRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday festival of parades and revelry, famously in New Orleans.

clue.text: Dad finds a right time to view Andy Warhol's work

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A father picks the right moment to go and see a Warhol exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s movement using images from mass culture, of which Warhol was the leading figure.

clue.text: Wealth of a criminal who has caught influenza

indicators.note: a person who has caught an illness holds it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods
flu is the short form of influenza

explanation.surface: A rich crook who has come down with the flu.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches and prosperity.

clue.text: Imagine an almost perfect note

indicators.note: almost means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Picture a musical note that is nearly flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: To form an idea of something in the mind; to conceive.

clue.text: Entertain the chaps at a bar, causing mirth

parts.note: to amuse is to entertain
chaps are men
T, the letter shaped like a crossbar, as in a T-bar

explanation.surface: Keeping the lads happy at the pub and getting laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places T after MEN; T stands for a bar because of its shape (a T-bar).
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter and enjoyment at something funny.

clue.text: Articles in three languages on my German battle

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
a is the English indefinite article
la is the French feminine word for the
mein is German for my

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in several languages, ending with a German possessive.
explanation.walkthrough: Three articles, Spanish EL, English A and French LA, are followed by German MEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1942 North African desert engagement where Montgomery defeated Rommel.

clue.text: Scone that was demolished by a bird

indicators.note: something demolished is broken up, so the letters of scone that are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scone that got eaten up by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird whose call sounds like two stones knocked together.

clue.text: Seek some tasks

indicators.note: some of means only part of the word tasks is used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Look for a few jobs to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To request or enquire after something.

clue.text: Five in motorist's club with surname Gardner

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star joins the motoring club among five members.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown-recovery club.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the 1940s and 50s Hollywood actress whose family name was Gardner.

clue.text: Give 1,000 pounds for a nap!

definitions.meaning: a unit of weight or force in engineering equal to a thousand pounds
a short sleep, in British slang

explanation.definitionFit: Both an engineers' unit of a thousand pounds' force and slang for a snooze.

clue.text: Did his cocktail parties go with a bang?

definitions.text: Did his cocktail parties go with a bang?

parts.words: Did his cocktail parties go with a bang?
parts.note: the cocktail is the improvised petrol bomb named after a Soviet foreign minister, which literally explodes

explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet minister whose name became attached to the improvised incendiary bomb.

clue.text: Metal superseding bronze for a time — a long time

parts.note: iron is a metal
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: History lesson: one metal replaced bronze, and it took ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The prehistoric period after the Bronze Age, when iron tools replaced bronze ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaeological era following the Bronze Age, when tools began to be made from a harder metal.

clue.text: Spring out at snake

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the synonym are put out of order

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Something leaps out at a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small venomous viper, as in Cleopatra's death.

clue.text: Captain catches first of season's herring

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the word season's

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: A ship's master lands the first herring of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The master of a ship or leader of a team.

clue.text: Saying goodbye like this seems to take forever!

definitions.text: Saying goodbye like this seems to take forever!

parts.words: Saying goodbye like this seems to take forever!
parts.note: an everyday farewell which, read word by word, also describes something lasting a great while

explanation.definitionFit: A casual farewell, literally meaning to such a great length.

clue.text: Agreement to draw line under account?

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed below the other piece

parts.note: a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: Drawing a line under an account to settle a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmony of opinion or a formal settlement between parties.

clue.text: Instruments played softly on the Sabbath

parts.note: piano is the musical direction meaning softly
S is an abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: A congregation's instruments are played quietly on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Large keyboard instruments with hammers striking strings.

clue.text: Cooked a woman!

parts.note: fried means cooked in fat

explanation.surface: A shocking cannibal exclamation: a woman has been cooked!
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as of the painter Kahlo, so a woman.

clue.text: The current plan

parts.note: current means electric flow, not present-day, so the plan is a wiring layout

explanation.definitionFit: The system of electrical connections laid out in a device.

clue.text: Girl is heartless, callous towards apes

parts.note: Mimi is a girl's name, as in La Bohème

indicators.note: heartless means the word callous loses all its inner letters, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: A girl without feeling behaves cruelly towards monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'towards' are link words; 'heartless' strips CALLOUS to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitates or copies, as a verb.

clue.text: A priest keen to be picked for job

parts.note: keen as in sharp, so pointed

explanation.surface: An eager priest wanting to be chosen for a post.
explanation.definitionFit: Named or selected for a position or office.

clue.text: African coins not applicable to rejected sari

indicators.note: rejected means the word sari is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A form note says the returned sari has nothing to do with African money.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency units of Nigeria.

clue.text: The shopkeeper is a mean darts player

indicators.note: a player plays with things, so the letters of mean darts are toyed with into a new order

explanation.surface: The local shop owner turns out to be a formidable darts player.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs a shop or follows a skilled trade.
